subject: Priority: suspected export flag & coordination — data transfer / forensics support
body:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@fintechco.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 08:12:04 -0700
Subject: Unusual export activity flagged — request for timeline & cooperation

Hi Nikhil,

We observed an unusual spike in outbound data egress from our integration with Redwood yesterday evening (approx. 02:40-03:10 UTC). Our security team flagged several exports containing partial customer identifiers. At this stage we can't determine if this is an operational sync or an accidental leakage from a connector.

Can your team confirm:
- Whether any scheduled or manual exports were run for FinTechCo within that window?
- What subprocessors (if any) might have handled those logs/backups?
- Whether Redwood can provide a sealed copy of the exported files and relevant access logs (S3 object names, timestamps, requester IPs) under an evidence hold?

We need an initial acknowledgment and proposed timeline for evidence collection within 24 hours, and a window for a deeper handover (forensics) within 72 hours. Please treat this as high priority.

Attaching the alert summary we shared from our SIEM.

Thanks,
Alice Monroe
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
FinTechCo

Attachment: fintechco_security_report_0310.pdf (summary PDF from SIEM)

---
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@fintechco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 09:05:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Unusual export activity flagged — request for timeline & cooperation

Alice — thanks for the heads up and the report. Acknowledged.

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
1) I'll spin up an evidence collection task and request S3/object manifests for the 02:00-04:00 UTC window.
2) Ben, can you triage whether any scheduled exports or admin-triggered transfers for FinTechCo ran then?
3) Marissa, please identify any subprocessors that would have handled logs/backups and whether we have retention/replication policies that could cause cross-region movement.

We commit to an initial package (manifests + redwood_log_manifest_0310.csv) within 24 hours and availability for a secure handover (read-only bucket or secure share) by EOD Monday, 72-hour target. If there is SLA-level escalation needed we can escalate to the incident desk.

I will not speculate on root cause until we have the artifacts. We will preserve all related objects under evidence hold and provide MD5s where possible.

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference

---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@fintechco.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Mar 2028 10:22:35 -0700
Subject: Re: Unusual export activity flagged — request for timeline & cooperation

Quick operational update:
- No scheduled periodic export job for FinTechCo is logged in the orchestrator between 02:00–04:00 UTC.
- I found two ad-hoc admin downloads initiated from a support token at 02:47 UTC; I am validating the requester identity and will confirm if it maps to a partner integration.
- Prepared the attached manifest (redwood_log_manifest_0310.csv) listing S3 keys, timestamps, byte sizes, and requester token hashes.

Marissa — please confirm subprocessors that could touch those objects (storage replication, backup agents, third-party forensics services). Jordan — can you standby for a read-only bucket handover if FinTechCo requests live forensic access?

Ben Carter
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_log_manifest_0310.csv

---
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@fintechco.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Mar 2028 16:45:12 -0700
Subject: RE: Unusual export activity flagged — request for timeline & cooperation

Alice/Nikhil/Team —

We have the initial artifacts ready for secure transfer. Proposed handover plan:
1) Evidence package (manifests + checksums) shared to a time-limited Cloud Storage folder and a sealed S3 bucket with read-only cross-account ACL for FinTechCo's forensic principal. Link below.
2) For formal chain-of-custody, we can sign an evidence transfer acknowledgment (template attached: forensics_readme.txt) and log all accesses.
3) Subprocessor note: the backup replication agent (ReplicateCo) may have a transient copy in eu-west-1 for redundancy; we will include the export paths and request their statement if FinTechCo needs one.

Please confirm which access model you prefer (drive link vs. cross-account read-only S3) and a point-of-contact for the forensics team. If FinTechCo wants us to push a copy into a temporary bucket under your account, we will coordinate the IAM role exchange and document the actions.

Jordan Blake
Lead, Forensic Response
Redwood Inference

Attachment: forensics_readme.txt (instructions and chain-of-custody template)

---
Notes:
- We preserved object keys and checksums; no objects have been deleted since detection.
- Preliminary scope indicates a small subset of rows with hashed customer identifiers; no clear plaintext PII observed yet.
- We flagged ReplicateCo as a subprocessors to query about potential EU replication.

Next actions requested from FinTechCo:
- Confirm preferred transfer method and POC for forensics (email or SSO principal).
- If you need a signed DPA addendum for expedited transfer, flag that and we will route to legal.

Document references: HubSpot:HS-45712, evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ABCxyz
